title: Approaches to prevent financial toxicity in cancer patients in Germany
summary:
As well as the physical and emotional strain, a cancer diagnosis can also lead to significant financial difficulties. In research, this financial burden is also referred to as ‘financial toxicity’. It can impair quality of life and adherence to treatment, exacerbate emotional stress and have a negative impact on the course of the disease. In Germany, cancer patients can find themselves under financial pressure despite having health insurance and access to existing social support services.
This can be due to both lower income and additional expenditure. During the course of the illness, patients themselves – or, for example, in the case of treating children with cancer or where there is a high need for care – their relatives may work less, either temporarily or permanently, and consequently lose income. At the same time, additional costs may arise, for example from co-payments for medicines, over-the-counter medicines, travel to treatment appointments or care. This can also increase the risk of excessive debt, potentially leading to insolvency. The situation can be particularly difficult if there is already little financial leeway at the time of diagnosis, for example due to a low income or existing debts. The type and stage of the cancer can also influence the financial burden.
The APRETOX project investigates how financial hardship resulting from a cancer diagnosis in Germany can be better prevented or addressed at an early stage. The project draws on a range of perspectives through interviews: from professionals in social work, cancer support services, hospital social services, rehabilitation clinics, health insurance funds and their professional associations, to cancer patients in debt and their relatives, and to cancer patients and their relatives receiving outpatient care. The project is supplemented by a survey of staff at debt and insolvency advice centres.
On this basis, a practical awareness-raising action plan to prevent financial hardship should be developed. The results will be presented to the public and, in collaboration with journalists and politicians, transformed into suitable information and educational materials. An advisory board comprising patients, another with experts and a third with public health representatives will accompany the project.
The aim of APRETOX is to identify gaps in the existing support structures for cancer patients and to highlight specific ways how those affected and their families can be better protected from the financial consequences of cancer and receive support at an early stage.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
WP 1: Social work staff in oncology, cancer counselling centres, hospital social services, rehabilitation clinics and health insurance funds; sufficient knowledge of German to have a conversation
WP 2: People who have or have had cancer and are in debt, or their relatives; sufficient knowledge of German to have a conversation
WP 3: People who have or have had cancer and are receiving outpatient care, or their relatives; sufficient knowledge of German to have a conversation
WP 4: Staff at debt and insolvency advice centres; sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
People under the age of 18, knowledge of German is insufficient for an interview
